objectives.text: Given the type and application of a direct current (DC) generator, DESCRIBE the operating characteristics of that generator including methods of voltage production, advantages of each type, and voltage-vs-load characteristics.

enabling.text: DEFINE terminal voltage as it applies to DC generators.
DEFINE counter-electromotive force (CEMF) as it applies to a DC machine.
DESCRIBE the effects of commutation in a DC generator.
STATE the purpose of each of the following components of a DC machine:
LIST the three conditions necessary to induce a voltage into a conductor.
Using the left-hand rule of generators, DETERMINE the direction of the magnetic field, the motion of the conductor, or the direction of current induced into a conductor.
DESCRIBE how terminal voltage of a DC generator is adjusted.
STATE the basis behind each of the four DC generator ratings.
LIST the four internal losses found in a DC generator.
DESCRIBE the differences in construction between a shunt-wound and a series-wound DC generator with respect to the relationship between the field and the armature.
DESCRIBE the relationship between the shunt and series fields for cumulatively- compounded and differentially-compounded DC generators.
DESCRIBE the voltage-vs-load current characteristics for a flat-compounded, over- compounded, and under-compounded DC generator.

passages.quote: Terminal voltage, as applied to DC generators, is defined as the voltage that can be measured at the output of the generator.
This induced voltage acts counter to applied voltage; therefore, it is called counter-electromotive force (CEMF).
commutation is the mechanical conversion from AC to DC at the brushes of a DC machine
The purpose of the armature is to provide the energy conversion in a DC machine
The purpose of the rotor is to provide the rotating element in a DC machine
The stator is the part of a motor or generator that is stationary
The purpose of the field in a DC machine is to provide a magnetic field for producing either a voltage (generator) or a torque (motor)
there are three conditions necessary to induce a voltage

point the index finger of your left hand in the direction of the magnetic field (from North to South) and point the thumb in the direction of motion of the conductor, the middle finger will point in the direction of current flow
The commutator converts the AC voltage generated in the rotating loop into a DC voltage.
This is the most widely used method for regulating the output voltage of a DC generator
A DC generator contains four ratings.
The current rating is based on the size of the conductor and the amount of heat that can be dissipated in the generator.
There are four internal losses that contribute to lower efficiency of a DC generator.
Copper loss is the power lost as heat in the windings
These circulating currents within the iron core are called eddy-currents.
the armature and field cores are constructed from laminated (layered) steel sheets.
When the field winding of a generator is connected in parallel with the generator armature, the generator is called a shunt-wound
When the field winding of a DC generator is connected in series with the armature, the generator is called a series-wound generator
A series generator has poor voltage regulation
If the two fields of a compound generator are wound so that their magnetic fields aid one another, the generator is said to be cumulatively-compounded.
If the two fields are wound so that their flux fields oppose one another, the generator is said to be differentially-compounded.
In practical compounded generators, the change in output voltage from no-load to full-load is less than 5 percent.
The output gradually rises with increasing load current over the normal operating range of the machine.
The output voltage decreases gradually with an increase in load current.

body.text: Applied voltage is the voltage that is delivered across the load. It should be the same as terminal voltage, but circuit faults and losses may reduce it.
In a generator with a rotating armature, voltage is induced in the armature conductors. It opposes the applied voltage and reduces the current flow through the armature.
Commutation is the positioning of the DC generator brushes so that the commutator segments change brushes at the same time the armature current changes direction.

checks.q: Where is the terminal voltage of a DC generator measured?
o: At the output of the generator
checks.x: Terminal voltage is defined as the voltage that can be measured at the output of the generator.

checks.q: What is counter-electromotive force in a DC machine?
o: The current in the field winding
An induced voltage that acts counter to applied voltage
checks.x: The voltage induced in the armature conductors acts counter to applied voltage, so it is called counter-electromotive force.

checks.q: What is the effect of commutation in a DC generator?
o: It converts AC to DC at the brushes
It converts DC to AC at the armature
checks.x: Commutation is the mechanical conversion from AC to DC at the brushes of a DC machine.

body.text: DC motors and generators have the same basic construction, differing primarily in the energy conversion.

body.alt: A basic DC machine in cutaway, with the stator, field, armature, rotor, brushes, and commutator segments labeled.

body.text: In a DC generator, the armature converts mechanical energy to electrical energy. In a DC motor, it converts electrical energy into mechanical energy in the form of torque.
In both types of DC machines, the rotor is the armature.
In DC machines, the purpose of the stator is to provide the magnetic field.
The field is produced by a permanent magnet or an electromagnet. Electromagnets are normally used because their magnetic strength is greater and more easily varied.

checks.q: What is the purpose of the armature in a DC machine?
o: To connect the brushes to the load
checks.x: The purpose of the armature is to provide the energy conversion in a DC machine.

checks.q: Which component is the stationary part of a DC machine?
checks.x: The stator is the part of a motor or generator that is stationary.

body.text: A basic DC generator has four basic parts: a magnetic field, a single conductor or loop, a commutator, and brushes.

body.cap: Basic Operation of a DC Generator
body.alt: A conductor loop rotating between north and south poles at two positions, with brushes on a commutator and the output voltage waveform.

body.text: The stronger the field or the more flux lines cut for a given period of time, the larger the induced EMF.

body.text: The voltage between the brushes fluctuates between zero and some maximum value, but is always of the same polarity.

body.text: Output voltage depends on the number of conductor loops in series in the armature, armature speed, and magnetic field strength.
The field strength can be changed quite easily by varying the current through the field winding.

checks.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three conditions necessary to induce a voltage into a conductor?
checks.x: The three conditions are a magnetic field, a conductor, and relative motion between the two.

checks.q: In the left-hand rule for generators, what does the middle finger show?
o: The direction of the magnetic field
checks.x: The index finger points along the magnetic field, the thumb along the motion of the conductor, and the middle finger along the current flow.

checks.q: What is the most widely used way to adjust the output voltage of a DC generator?
o: Changing the number of armature conductors
Varying the current through the field winding
checks.x: Varying the current through the field winding changes the field strength. This is the most widely used method for regulating the output voltage.

items: Voltage: based on the insulation type and design of the machine.
Current: based on the size of the conductor and the amount of heat that can be dissipated in the generator.
Power: based on the mechanical limitations of the device that turns the generator, and on the thermal limits of conductors, bearings, and other components.
Speed: the upper limit is the speed at which mechanical damage is done, and the lower limit is based on the limit for field current.

body.text: Hysteresis losses occur when the armature rotates in a magnetic field. Rotating magnetic domains in the iron cause friction and heat.
Mechanical losses can be caused by bearing friction, brush friction on the commutator, or air friction called windage.

checks.q: What is the current rating of a DC generator based on?
o: The speed that causes mechanical damage
The size of the conductor and the heat that can be dissipated
checks.x: The current rating is based on the size of the conductor and the amount of heat that can be dissipated in the generator.

checks.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four internal losses of a DC generator?
checks.x: The four internal losses are copper, eddy-current, hysteresis, and mechanical losses.

body.alt: Shunt-wound DC generator: the field winding connected in parallel with the armature, shown as a schematic and as a machine.

body.text: A shunt-wound generator has a much more stable voltage output than a series-wound generator.
As load current increases, the voltage drop across the armature coil increases, so output voltage decreases. The field current then decreases, which lowers voltage further.

body.cap: Output Voltage-vs-Load Current for Shunt-Wound DC Generator
body.alt: Graph of terminal voltage against load current for a shunt-wound generator, falling gently to full-load current.
Series-wound DC generator: the field winding connected in series with the armature, shown as a schematic and as a machine.

body.text: The excitation current in a series-wound generator is the same as the current the generator delivers to the load.

body.alt: Graph of terminal voltage against load current for a series-wound generator, rising steeply with load current.

body.text: As a result, series generators are not used for fluctuating loads.

checks.q: How is the field winding connected in a shunt-wound DC generator?
o: Across the brushes in series with the load
checks.x: When the field winding is connected in parallel with the generator armature, the generator is called a shunt-wound generator.

checks.q: In a series-wound generator, what current flows through the field winding?
o: The same current the generator delivers to the load
checks.x: The excitation current in a series-wound generator is the same as the current the generator delivers to the load.

body.text: A compound generator has a field winding in parallel with the armature and a field winding in series with it.

body.alt: A series generator and a shunt generator combined into a compounded DC generator with both field windings.

body.text: As load current increases in a cumulatively-compounded generator, the series field strength increases and compensates for the decrease in shunt field strength.
A generator with this characteristic is said to be flat-compounded.
In an over-compounded generator, the series winding overcompensates for a change in the shunt field.
In an under-compounded generator, the series winding undercompensates for the change in shunt field strength.

body.cap: Voltage-vs-Current for a Compounded DC Generator
body.alt: Graph of output voltage against load current with three curves: over-compounded rising, flat-compounded nearly level, and under-compounded falling.

checks.q: In a cumulatively-compounded generator, how do the two fields act?
o: Only the shunt field is used
checks.x: If the two fields are wound so that their magnetic fields aid one another, the generator is cumulatively-compounded.

checks.q: How much does the output voltage of a flat-compounded generator change from no-load to full-load?
checks.x: In practical compounded generators, the change in output voltage from no-load to full-load is less than 5 percent.

checks.q: What happens to the output of an over-compounded generator as load current increases?
checks.x: The output gradually rises with increasing load current over the normal operating range of the machine.

examples.title: Raising terminal voltage
examples.problem: The output voltage of an operating DC generator must be raised. Which of the three factors should change?
steps: The number of conductors cannot be changed in a normally operating generator.
It is usually impractical to change the armature speed.
The magnetic field strength can be changed easily by varying the field winding current.
examples.answer: Vary the current through the field winding

summary.text: Terminal voltage is the voltage that can be measured at the output of the generator.
In a DC generator, commutation provides for the conversion of AC to a DC output that is generated in the armature windings.
The armature provides the energy conversion, the rotor is the rotating element, and the field provides a magnetic field.
A voltage is induced when there is a magnetic field, a conductor, and relative motion between the two.
The terminal voltage of a DC generator is adjusted by varying the field strength.
A shunt-wound generator has its field in parallel with the armature winding, and its voltage decreases with an increase in load.
A series-wound generator has its field in series with the armature winding, and its voltage increases sharply with an increase in load.
In a cumulatively-compounded generator the fields aid one another, and in a differentially-compounded generator they oppose one another.

The chapter puts CEMF in a generator, while the summary calls it a voltage that counters applied voltage in a DC motor or a DC generator. The lesson uses the chapter wording.
